extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers; policymakers and defense industry
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper report summarizing the National Defense Advisory Commission's general principles and labor policy guidance for letting U.S. national defense contracts and related procurement/industrial measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed of delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Speed of delivery of all items on the defense program is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders should be placed to ensure the most efficient use of each facility from the viewpoint of the program as a whole; proper consideration should be given to contributory industries (e.g., machine-tool industry) to avoid creating bottlenecks; once delivery dates are fixed, assurance must be given that they will be met by the supplier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper quality is of prime importance and must be determined before awarding contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the supplier can meet the quality requirements as specified; suppliers should be willing to adjust specifications cooperatively so they come as near as possible to commercial standards while still meeting military needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Price — secure a fair price
rubrics_metrics.description: Price, while not the sole consideration, is of outstanding significance and every effort must be made to secure a fair price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Price decisions must take recognition of proper cost factors; however, in emergency defense contexts, speed and delivery considerations may outweigh price alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of consumers' needs
rubrics_metrics.description: The impact of the defense program upon consumers must be a factor in procurement decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give due regard to protecting civilian needs and morale; ensure proper health and housing conditions among employees; consider off-season production to dovetail military and civilian requirements, which can lower overhead and prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate consideration of labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequate consideration must be given to labor in the conduct of the defense program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Means compliance with the labor principles adopted by the commission (Aug. 31 release), including recognized labor standards, and using employment services when appropriate; labor safeguards contribute to efficient production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with labor statutes and safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Work carried on as part of the defense program should comply with applicable Federal and local labor statutory provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to Walsh-Healey Act, Fair Labor Standards Act, National Labor Relations Act, and local statutes affecting labor relations, hours, wages, workers’ compensation, safety, sanitation, etc.; adequate provisions must be made for employee health and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid undue geographic concentration of orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Undue geographic concentration of defense orders should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid concentrating procurement both by procurement districts and by industrial sections to reduce vulnerability and distributional problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial responsibility of the supplier
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the financial responsibility of prospective suppliers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ability to post a bond is not alone sufficient; preference should be given to suppliers able to finance themselves through private sources rather than requiring government aid; financial capacity is a factor in award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive bidding preferred; negotiated contracts allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive bidding is generally the better procedure, but negotiated contracts may be authorized where competitive bidding will not fulfill defense needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend competitive bidding where appropriate; permit negotiated contracts when necessary to meet program objectives, speed, or special circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral responsibility and reputation of supplier
rubrics_metrics.description: The moral responsibility and general standing of the supplier are important qualification factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence of honest and sincere desire to cooperate (produce on time without profiteering), willingness to assume some risks, and accurate statements of capacity and experience; reputation among reputable business men is an index of qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of congestion in transport and warehousing
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid congestion of transportation and warehousing facilities in planning procurement and distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procurement placements should consider transport and warehousing capacity to prevent bottlenecks that would slow delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of power facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Due consideration should be given to the adequacy of power facilities, particularly where provided by public utilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess local power infrastructure when selecting sites or awarding contracts that depend on reliable electricity supply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for firms experienced with related orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Give general preference to firms having experience with so-called educational orders (i.e., prior similar defense/educational production).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experience with comparable orders is a favorable factor in awarding contracts because it indicates ability to meet requirements promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work hours, overtime, and employee welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts should be made to avoid hours in excess of forty a week; overtime policies and employee welfare must be respected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When defense requirements necessitate excess hours or weekend work, overtime should be paid according to local recognized practices; in emergencies some excess may be permitted but reasonable hours, fair working conditions, and proper wages are essential to efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of employment services and absorption of surplus labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize employment services and make efforts to absorb surplus and unemployed labor into the defense program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection of plant locations and production planning should consider employment benefits and avoid unnecessary disruption of social safeguards (nondiscrimination by sex, race, color; provide adequate housing facilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Government takeover authority for non-cooperative industry
rubrics_metrics.description: If a manufacturer refuses government defense orders or priority, the Government may take over the plant and operate it on a fair rental basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The law provides for government operation and penalties for noncompliance; this is a backstop to ensure fulfillment of defense program needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reemployment protection for conscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers are enjoined to restore jobs to former conscripts unless impossible or unreasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an employer refuses to reinstate a former conscript, he is liable to court action — a protection intended to mitigate defense mobilization’s impact on workers.
